title: Volume 3 · Supplier Reality: Returns, Advances and Landed Cost
subtitle: Lessons 5–8: debit notes, advance payments, landed cost allocation and the ageing conversation every client has in week three
outcomes: Return faulty goods and reverse both stock and tax correctly
Handle an advance payment without leaving a permanent unallocated balance
Push freight and duty into stock value so gross profit tells the truth
Read supplier ageing and explain it to a business owner in one page

slides.title: Return one damaged blender without breaking the books
bullets: A return reverses the receipt first, then the bill, which is the order auditors expect
ERPNext creates a debit note from the purchase invoice, so tax reverses with the goods
Return to Returns Quarantine rather than straight to Main, so the goods are visibly excluded
Never edit the original receipt; a return is a new document with its own number
slides.notes: Doing the return before the debit note is what keeps the stock ledger and the ledger in step. If you reverse the bill first, the stock sits in quarantine with no matching liability and the audit trail needs a manual explanation. Practise the sequence until it is automatic, because the first live return will happen under pressure, minutes before the client's month-end cut-off.

slides.title: Nine units, and the tax comes back with them
bullets: Stock falls by the returned quantity at its original valuation
The debit note reduces the creditor and reverses the input tax proportionally
The supplier's balance now shows a credit that can offset the next invoice
Returned goods in quarantine are still owned, so they remain in stock value
slides.notes: The debit note total of 132.00 is the one number to make the learner predict, because it proves they understand that tax follows goods. If they say 120.00, they have not seen that a return reverses input tax as well as stock. Make them compute it before opening the debit note, then let them compare.

slides.title: Pay before delivery without losing the money
bullets: An advance is a payment with no invoice, recorded as a liability to the supplier
ERPNext tracks it as Advance Paid, which reduces the outstanding on the next bill
Leave Payment References empty: an advance is proved by Unallocated Amount in the Writeoff section
Allocate the advance to the invoice, otherwise it sits forever as an unexplained credit
The advance appears separately on the balance sheet until it is consumed

rows: Payment type Pay, party Sunrise Components
Bank side of the form complete
Advance Paid 660.00 on the supplier record

slides.notes: Advances are where cash leaves before paperwork exists, which is exactly the situation that produces month-end surprises. The empty Payment References table is correct here and worth saying out loud, because learners expect an allocation and try to create one. Show the supplier ledger before and after allocation: before, a 660.00 debit with the whole amount sitting as unallocated; after, zero. If they can explain that movement, they can explain any advance query the client's finance team raises.

slides.title: Put the freight into the stock, not into an expense
bullets: Landed cost allocates freight, duty and clearing charges across the received units
Without it, gross profit is overstated and every margin report lies by the freight amount
Allocation can be by quantity, amount or weight, and the choice must match the business
The voucher creates a stock ledger revaluation and a matching GL entry
slides.notes: Freight of 60.00 across ten units gives 6.00 each, and valuation moves from 120.00 to 126.00. The moment a learner computes that, they can also explain why the margin on a 240.00 sale is 114.00 rather than 120.00. Landed cost is the single most requested report fix in distribution projects, because owners compare gross profit to their own mental arithmetic.

slides.title: Bundle supplier payments without losing the allocation
bullets: A payment order groups the invoices you intend to pay on one date, so the bank sees one instruction
Every line must carry its invoice reference, or the allocation is lost when the file is produced
Each generated payment entry shows its settlement in the Reference section as a Payment References row
Payment orders are optional, but they leave an audit trail that a single manual payment cannot
Reconcile the total before submitting, because a payment order posts real bank entries
slides.notes: Payment orders are the difference between a payment run that takes ten minutes and one that takes an afternoon. Show the learner the generated payment entries and their allocations, because that is the evidence the bank file and the ledger agree. If a client insists on manual payments, at minimum insist on allocation, or the supplier ageing will drift from the bank within a month.

slides.title: What the revaluation does to the margin
bullets: Landed cost is only useful if the reports downstream pick up the new valuation
Gross profit compares selling price to the revalued cost, not the purchase rate
The offsetting entry goes to the expense account you nominated, so freight is not double counted
Recompute one sale by hand and compare it with the report before showing the client
slides.notes: The point of this check is that the learner can defend the margin number in front of an owner who does the arithmetic in their head. Two hundred forty less one hundred twenty six is one hundred fourteen, and a ten per cent discount leaves ninety. If the report says otherwise, the landed cost was posted after the margin report date or allocated by amount instead of quantity.

slides.title: Supplier documents and what each one fixes
bullets: Every remedy is a document with a number, never an edit to history
Debit notes reverse goods and tax together, keeping the match intact
Advances are consumed by allocation, not by journal entry
Landed cost changes valuation, so it must be posted before the margin report is trusted

rows: Goods go back to the supplier
Supplier owes you money or goods
Returning only part of the tax
Freight, duty or clearing arrives after receipt
Allocating by amount when units differ

slides.notes: Treat this page as the remedy list for a support call. Each row answers a question a client will ask in the first month: the goods came back, the supplier wants money up front, freight arrived late. If a consultant can name the document without looking it up, the client stops worrying about the migration.

slides.title: Supplier ageing, read properly
bullets: Ageing buckets answer when money leaves, not whether the bill is correct
An invoice with no due date lands in the oldest bucket and distorts the whole report
Advances and debit notes appear as negatives, which is correct and often misread
Reconcile the ageing total to the creditor control account before presenting it

rows: General Ledger, Stock Received But Not Billed

slides.notes: Presenting supplier ageing to an owner is a consultant skill, not a report skill. Lead with total payable, confirm it ties to the control account, then explain that the older bucket is a cash conversation rather than an accounting error. When the interim account is not zero, a receipt is unbilled, and that is the only real finding worth raising.

lab.title: Lab · Return, advance, land the cost and read the ageing
steps: Return one damaged blender to Returns Quarantine and record the return receipt number
Raise the debit note from the purchase invoice and confirm the 132.00 total
Compute the new stock value at Main and check it against Stock Balance
Record a 660.00 advance payment to Sunrise Components from the bank
Create the 660.00 invoice and allocate the advance against it
Post a landed cost voucher for 60.00 freight across the received units
Confirm the new valuation per unit and recompute the gross profit on a 240.00 sale
Open supplier ageing and tie the total to the creditors control account
lab.done: Done when Main holds 9 units at 126.00 each, the supplier has no unallocated advance, and the ageing total equals the creditors control balance to the cent.

quiz.question: In which order should a purchase return be handled?
quiz.why: Reversing stock first keeps the stock ledger and the accounting ledger in step, and the debit note then reverses the matching creditor and tax amounts.

quiz.question: A debit note for one blender at 120.00 with 10 % tax totals what?
quiz.why: Goods of 120.00 plus 12.00 input tax reverses 132.00 against the supplier, because tax follows the goods out of the business.

quiz.question: How is an advance payment cleared against an invoice?
options: By allocating it in the payment or invoice
quiz.why: ERPNext keeps advances as unallocated amounts and consumes them when you allocate against an invoice, which is what keeps the supplier ledger clean.

quiz.question: Landed cost of 60.00 across 10 units changes valuation to what?
quiz.why: Freight is spread over quantity, so 6.00 per unit is added to the 120.00 purchase rate. Gross profit on a 240.00 sale becomes 114.00.

quiz.question: What does a non-zero Stock Received But Not Billed balance indicate?
options: A receipt that has not been billed
quiz.why: The interim account clears when the purchase invoice is submitted, so any remaining balance means at least one receipt is still waiting for its bill.

memory.spine: Reverse in the order you posted, put freight into the stock rather than the expense column, and let the allocation do the work.

device.label: Reverse in the order you posted
expansion: A return reverses the receipt first and the bill second, which is the order auditors expect
An advance is a payment with no invoice, so it is a liability until it is allocated
Landed cost allocates freight, duty and clearing into the stock valuation, not the profit and loss
A payment order groups invoices due on one date so the bank sees one instruction
Every remedy is a new document with a number, and history is never edited

cards.q: One damaged unit goes back to the supplier. In what order?
cards.a: The goods return first, then the bill adjustment, so stock and tax reverse together.

cards.q: How is an advance to a supplier recorded?
cards.a: A payment entry with no allocation against an invoice, so it stays a liability rather than an expense.
In a Landed Cost Voucher, allocated across the received units and revaluing the stock they sit in.

cards.q: What must be true after a landed cost allocation?
cards.a: The downstream margin reports actually use the new valuation, otherwise the allocation is decoration.

cards.q: What do ageing buckets tell you?
cards.a: When money leaves, not whether the bill is correct. Correctness is the three way match.

trap.what: Freight is booked straight to an expense because the landed cost voucher looks like extra work.
trap.why: The cost lands once, stock stays under valued, and every later sale reports a margin that cannot be defended.

narration: Suppliers rarely behave the way the process diagram says. They deliver late, send one damaged unit, ask for money before the goods arrive, and send the freight invoice a fortnight afterwards. Each of those has one right document. A return reverses stock first, then the debit note reverses the creditor and the tax, which is why nine units remain at one hundred twenty six each. An advance is money without an invoice, consumed by allocation rather than by a journal, otherwise it sits on the balance sheet forever and the client's auditor asks why. And landed cost is what turns a one hundred twenty rate into a one hundred twenty six valuation, so a two hundred forty sale earns one hundred fourteen rather than one hundred twenty, and the owner's own arithmetic finally agrees with the report. Get those three right and the supplier ageing conversation becomes arithmetic instead of an argument, which is exactly the conversation a distribution client wants to have in week three.
